source_snapshot.procedure: Run IPMI OOB `power reset` repeatedly for 24 hours while keeping SOL connected; source setup requests log clearing.
source_snapshot.criteria: SOL always connected, BMC functional after stress, no stress errors in SEL/OS logs, and correct FRU/SDR on every cycle.
source_snapshot.script: Private hard-reset; 30 attended and 1500 machine minutes.

historical_reviews.deepseek: Correctly identifies the maintenance risk but the illustrative loop lacks secure credential handling, exact readiness gates, per-cycle recovery or evidence, and a tested abort path.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Correctly retains the 24-hour stress objective while requiring approval, target isolation, controlled reset/recovery, operator SOL observation, preserved logs and per-cycle FRU/SDR validation.
historical_reviews.history: No earlier exact source identity record exists.
historical_reviews.v3_1: A hard reset necessarily interrupts host execution and may disrupt SOL transport. `Always connected` must therefore be evaluated as an owner-defined disconnect/reconnect and console-continuity contract for every reset, not as a literal uninterrupted TCP session or a single final connectivity check.

original_test_intent: Stress a dedicated SUT with repeated OOB hard resets for 24 hours and verify per-cycle SOL recovery, BMC functionality, clean SEL/OS behavior and stable FRU/SDR data.
original_method: After rehearsal and explicit approval, issue one supported reset at a time, enforce bounded BMC/IPMI/LAN/OS and boot recovery, record SOL disconnect/reconnect against the approved contract, compare per-cycle FRU/SDR and preserved event deltas, and stop on any anomaly without automatic retry.
manual_activity: The owner approves target isolation, 24-hour duration, reset interval, reconnect and abort semantics; an operator observes SOL/KVM recovery and owns anomaly handling and the final verdict.
required_inputs: Supported IPMI hard-reset method and cipher
Stable OOB recovery and operator coverage
safety_requirements: Perform one reset at a time
Verify identity and full recovery before the next cycle
Preserve logs and reset-caused console evidence
Never run on production or shared systems
Stop on timeout, identity drift, BMC instability, data warning or FRU/SDR drift
Do not automatically retry an ambiguous reset
agent_execution_scope: Verify target and approved stress contract
Run one approved reset cycle at a time
Poll bounded management and host recovery
Capture SOL reconnect timing and operator observations
Collect per-cycle FRU/SDR and event deltas
Enforce hard duration and abort rules
Report complete cycle ledger without verdict
engineer_actions: Approve reset method and stop thresholds
Review any console, event or FRU/SDR anomaly

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: `ipmitool power reset` matches the reset operation, but the one-shot and sample loop do not satisfy the 24-hour per-cycle evidence contract and expose command-line credentials without bounded recovery or abort handling.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use a secret-safe supported IPMI reset runner that issues one cycle only after prior recovery is proven, with bounded polls, per-cycle evidence capture and a tested immediate stop path.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The 24-hour objective, 30 attended/1500 machine minutes and per-cycle FRU/SDR criteria remain; blanket log clearing is excluded and SOL continuity is made measurable as reconnect semantics.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Maintain a cycle ledger with reset acknowledgement, management/host recovery milestones, SOL disconnect/reconnect, boot completion, FRU/SDR hashes, event deltas, retries and abort decision.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds secure orchestration, explicit recovery gates, measurable SOL semantics and complete per-cycle evidence instead of an open loop and final reachability check.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A single reset or command success cannot establish 24-hour durability, console recovery or per-cycle inventory integrity.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Repeated resets can expose data integrity, boot-loop and management failures; visual SOL/KVM quality and resume decisions remain engineer-owned.

project_override_considerations: The Project must supply target-specific recovery deadlines, reset interval, SOL semantics, FRU/SDR comparison rules and stop thresholds. Power removal, configuration changes and log clearing remain outside this hard-reset case.
expected_evidence: Owner approval, exact target, reset/cipher and recovery contract
One-cycle rehearsal and tested abort path
Per-cycle reset response and BMC/IPMI/LAN/OS/boot timings
Per-cycle FRU/SDR comparison and preserved SEL/OS deltas
Final duration, cycle count, health, anomaly and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently describe hard-reset stress and per-cycle health. Literal `SOL always connected` is an underspecified recovery oracle resolved by owner-approved reconnect semantics, not a competing source scope.

blocked_analysis.analysis: A normal stress harness, dedicated target, recovery contract and operator coverage can be provided. Execution blocks if those controls or explicit 24-hour approval are unavailable, or if any cycle becomes ambiguous.

review_improvement: Converts an unsafe 24-hour reset loop into gated cycles with observable recovery, explicit SOL semantics, preserved diagnostics and immediate stop behavior.
independent_technical_reasoning: A reset acknowledgement only shows the BMC accepted a command. The meaningful state transition spans host reset assertion, management reachability, firmware/boot progression, OS readiness and console reattachment. Advancing the loop before those milestones can stack failures and destroy causal evidence, so each cycle must be closed with inventory and event checks before the next begins.
